newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez board approved merger terms - source.
newsitem.headline: Suez board approved merger terms - source.

text.p: The supervisory board of Cie de Suez has unanimously agreed that the company would be merged into utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux through a swap of 20 Lyonnaise shares for 41 Suez stock, a source close to the discussions said on Friday.

Suez earlier said in a statement it would put the merger plan before its shareholders on June 11 for approval. It will pay a dividend of 24.6 francs ($4.24) per share, or a total 3.8 billion francs, as a sweetener to shareholders.
The dividend figure, which compared with 8.2 francs for 1995, includes a special payment to reflect the capital gain made on the sale of Banque Indosuez to Credit Agricole.
Lyonnaise des Eaux Chairman Jerome Monod and Suez Chairman Gerard Mestrallet are scheduled to announce the details of their merger plan at a news conference starting 1630 GMT.
The merger of the two companies will create a group with sales of 200 billion francs and a market value of 3.8 billion francs. ($ = 5.789 French Francs)
